nodes.label: CI job: backend-tests (pytest unit tests, no DB)
nodes.rationale: Pure unit tests using fake repositories; no Postgres/.env needed since settings() only fails fast when DEBUG=false, and the default is true when env vars are unset.

nodes.label: CI job: backend-lint (ruff check)
nodes.rationale: Only ruff check is run, not ruff format — formatting (Black-style) is deliberately not enforced here.

nodes.label: CI job: backend-integration-tests (real Postgres)
nodes.rationale: Spins up real Postgres to verify EXCLUDE USING gist double-booking guard, partial unique indexes for soft-deleted rows, and full HTTP-stack happy paths that fake-repository unit tests cannot exercise.

nodes.label: CI job: frontend-build (npm run build + npm audit)
CI job: frontend-e2e (Playwright against real backend+Postgres)
nodes.rationale: Catches things unit/integration tests cannot: real HTTP redirects and races between router guards and async store updates — found and fixed two real bugs this way (SetupWizard missing auth.ready, DashboardLayout/AppHeader not awaiting auth.logout() before redirect).

nodes.label: CI job: frontend-lint (eslint only)
nodes.rationale: Only eslint runs, not prettier --check — full autoformatting deliberately not forced.

nodes.label: CI job: compose-validate (docker compose config syntax check)
nodes.rationale: Uses dummy SECRET_KEY/SETUP_TOKEN values only to validate docker-compose.yml syntax/interpolation, not for a real run.

nodes.label: pip-audit exception: PYSEC-2026-1325 (ecdsa)
nodes.rationale: Only known vulnerability with no upstream fix; not exploitable because ecdsa is a transitive dependency of python-jose used only for RSA/EC algorithms, while this app signs JWTs exclusively with HS256 (symmetric HMAC).

nodes.label: npm audit continue-on-error exception (esbuild/vite dev-server findings)
nodes.rationale: Current high/moderate findings (path traversal etc. in vite's dev server) only affect `npm run dev`, not the deployed static build. Proper fix is a major vite 5→8 upgrade, deliberately deferred; step kept visible (not removed) to catch new findings on top of the known ones.
